kurz: Every indicator is a calculation rule applied to the same price series, and its formula shows in advance what it cannot achieve.

bloecke.md:
An indicator measures nothing in the market. It is a function that converts one known series of numbers into another. Even before any interpretation, it is therefore clear that it can only contain information already present in price and volume. RSI, MACD, Bollinger Bands, stochastics and ATR are transformations of the same input data. They condense existing information; they do not generate new information.

This leads to the most important practical consequence. If you apply three oscillators to the same price series and wait until they agree, you are counting the same information three times. The indicators agree because they are calculated from the same source. They do not provide independent evidence that adds up.

bloecke.titel: Four indicators from one data source
bloecke.unter: On the left are the data of a chart, on the right the well-known indicators, and the calculation steps in between consist only of averages and differences.

bloecke.md:
## Daily change in the moving average

The simple moving average over n periods is the mean of the last n closing prices. Its change from one day to the next depends on only two prices, today's and the one that drops out of the window today. This property is rarely mentioned explicitly.

bloecke.erklaerung: The slope of a moving average is the difference between the newly added price and the price dropping out, divided by the length of the window.
variablen: length of the window in periods
closing price that drops out of the window today

bloecke.titel: Average rises without any price movement
bloecke.md:
A share closes today, as it did yesterday, at €80.00. The closing price from 200 trading days ago was €74.00 and drops out of the window today.

Change in the SMA(200) = (80.00 − 74.00) / 200 = +€0.03.

The average rises even though the price has not moved by a single cent today. This happens regularly with crossover signals. A golden cross can be triggered simply because a low price from ten months ago drops out of the calculation.

## The exponential moving average

The exponential moving average (EMA) gives the greatest weight to the latest price and geometrically decreasing weights to older prices. By common convention, the smoothing factor is tied to the number of periods so that EMA(n) and SMA(n) are comparable.

bloecke.formel: EMA_t = α × P_t + (1 − α) × EMA_(t−1)     with α = 2 / (n + 1)
bloecke.erklaerung: The EMA is a weighted average of the current price and its own previous value. The coupling α = 2/(n+1) is chosen so that EMA(n) and SMA(n) have the same average lag of (n−1)/2 periods.
variablen: closing price of the current period
bloecke.beispiel: EMA(200): α = 2/201 ≈ 0.00995. Around 13.5% of the total weight falls on prices older than 200 periods. In the EMA, even very old prices keep some weight, whereas the SMA leaves out values outside its window entirely.

bloecke.titel: Average lag, calculated exactly from the formula
zeilen: in addition to the lag of the MACD line
approx. two and a half weeks

bloecke.md: Lag is a property of all causal filters and therefore also occurs with well-constructed indicators. A value formed as a weighted average of past prices with non-negative weights inevitably lags behind the price. Constructions advertised as having “zero lag” achieve this only with negative weights on older values. They reduce the lag at the cost of increased noise and gain no predictive power in the process.

bloecke.unter: Illustrative calculation over 30 periods with a rise up to period 15 and a subsequent decline. Price, SMA(10) and EMA(10) are calculated exactly from the series; the price turns at 121.00, the SMA only five periods later.

bloecke.md:
This calculation yields three findings that you can check by counting in the chart. First, SMA(10) and EMA(10) lie exactly on top of each other during the steady rise, both at 114.25 in period 15. The coupling α = 2/(n+1) ensures this. Second, the price reaches its high in period 15, the EMA turns in period 19 and the SMA only in period 20. Third, the price falls below the SMA in period 19, which triggers a sell signal at 116.20, 3.97% below the high of 121.00. With the EMA, the same signal comes one period later, even though the EMA turned earlier.

Which filter triggers faster therefore depends on the price path and not on a property of the filter. That is why comparisons such as “EMA is better than SMA” are worthless without stating the period tested.

If the SMA(50) crosses the SMA(200) from below, this is called a golden cross, and in the opposite direction a death cross. Mathematically, the signal compares a centre of gravity lying about five weeks back with one lying about twenty weeks back. Between them lie 75 trading days. The signal is a statement about the past that is formulated today. It can be informative but does not provide a forecast.

## The RSI and the threshold of 70

For the relative strength index (RSI), Wilder forms separate averages of the upward and downward movements over 14 periods and puts them in relation to each other. The usual notation `RSI = 100 − 100/(1+RS)` does not reveal how simple the quantity is. Rearranged algebraically, it becomes a proportion formula.

bloecke.formel: RSI = 100 × Avg gain / (Avg gain + Avg loss)
bloecke.erklaerung: The RSI is the proportion of the average upward movement in the total movement of the last 14 periods. The formula is identical to the standard formula but easier to read. Following Wilder, the averages are updated as (previous value × 13 + current value) / 14, and thus differently from a simple average.
variablen: smoothed average of the up days, with down days counting as 0
smoothed average of the down days as positive amounts

bloecke.titel: Ratio of movements at each RSI level
bloecke.unter: Exact inversion of the formula: ratio = RSI/(100−RSI). Between 30 and 70 the ratio changes little, above 80 it rises steeply; the RSI is therefore not a linear scale.

serien.name: Avg gain per 1 unit of avg loss

bloecke.md:
With the proportion formula, the threshold of 70 can be interpreted directly. It means that the average up day of the last 14 periods was 2.33 times as large as the average down day. This describes the past course and is not a statement about valuation, fundamentals or probability. The word “overbought” is an interpretation; all that is measured is the ratio of the movements. In a stable uptrend, the RSI can stay above 70 for weeks without the formula reaching a limit.

Mathematically, Wilder smoothing with the factor 1/14 corresponds to an EMA(27). The RSI(14) therefore has a memory of around 27 periods and an average lag of 13 periods. It thus reacts considerably more sluggishly than the figure “14” suggests.

Starting position after 14 periods: avg gain 1.00, avg loss 0.50. The ratio is 2.0, so RSI = 100 × 1.00/1.50 = 66.7.

Day 15 closes 2.00 higher:
Avg gain = (1.00 × 13 + 2.00)/14 = 1.071 · Avg loss = (0.50 × 13 + 0)/14 = 0.464 · RSI = 69.8

Day 16 closes 3.00 lower:
Avg gain = (1.071 × 13)/14 = 0.995 · Avg loss = (0.464 × 13 + 3.00)/14 = 0.645 · RSI = 60.7

A single down day of 3.00 units lowers the RSI by 9.1 points, an up day of 2.00 units raises it by 3.1 points. The damping by 13/14 does not explain this asymmetry, because it reduces both averages in the same proportion and on its own does not change the RSI. The asymmetry has two causes. At 3.00, the down day is larger than the up day at 2.00, and with an RSI above 50 the average loss is smaller than the average gain, so a new loss moves the RSI more than a gain of the same size.

## MACD as the difference between two averages

The MACD line is the difference EMA(12) − EMA(26) of the closing prices. The signal line is an EMA(9) of this line, and the histogram is the difference between the two. The standard parameters 12/26/9 go back to Gerald Appel, who developed the MACD in the late 1970s. It is often said that they date from the time of the six-day trading week and correspond to two weeks, one month and one and a half weeks. The timing does not fit, as there has been no Saturday trading on the New York Stock Exchange since 1952, and no other substantive derivation of the values is documented. Nor is there any robust evidence that other values would be better.

bloecke.titel: Zero line and moving average crossover
bloecke.md: The MACD line is zero exactly when EMA(12) and EMA(26) are equal. The MACD crossing the zero line and the two averages crossing each other are therefore the same event in two displays. Counting both as two confirmations counts the same event twice.

## Bollinger Bands

The middle band is the SMA(20). The bands lie two standard deviations above and below it, calculated from the same 20 values using the population formula. These parameters have been unchanged for over 35 years. It is often concluded from this that, with two standard deviations, around 95% of all cases lie within the bands. That does not apply here, for two reasons. The standard deviation comes from the same 20 observations as the mean, so it describes only this window and does not estimate a fixed distribution. In addition, returns have fatter tails than the normal distribution assumes.

Illustrative calculation: 19 closing prices are exactly 100.00, one day closes at 109.00.

Mean = 100.45 · standard deviation (population formula) = 1.96 · bands at 96.53 and 104.37 · BandWidth = 7.8% of the middle band.

Without this one day, the standard deviation would be zero and the bands would lie on the middle band. Exactly 20 trading days later, the outlier drops out of the window and the bands contract without the price having moved. A narrowing of the bands is therefore never a signal on its own, because it can be a pure artefact of the calculation window.

## Average true range

The true range is the largest of three distances and therefore also captures price gaps that are missing from a pure high-low range. The ATR is its Wilder-smoothed average and measures swings, not direction.

bloecke.formel:
TR = max( High − Low, |High − Previous close|, |Low − Previous close| )
ATR(14) = (ATR_previous × 13 + TR) / 14
bloecke.erklaerung: Thanks to the three candidates, an opening gap is not lost. The ATR is an amount in price units and not a percentage. It can only be compared between different instruments after dividing by the price.
bloecke.beispiel: Previous close 50.00; today high 48.60, low 47.50. High − Low = 1.10, but |Low − Previous close| = 2.50. The TR is 2.50 and is thus more than twice as large as the visible daily range.

bloecke.md: Since the ATR indicates no direction, it is not suitable as a buy or sell signal, but it is suitable as a yardstick for distances. One example is two shares at €50.00 each, one with an ATR(14) of €1.20, the other with €0.40. The same rule, “stop two ATRs below entry”, gives €47.60 in one case, a distance of 4.8%, and €49.20 in the other, a distance of 1.6%. This adjustment to volatility is the purpose of the rule, as a fixed percentage distance would treat both the same, even though one moves three times as much as the other. How the number of shares follows from this is covered in the lesson on risk management.

## Parameter optimisation and multiple testing

Every indicator has parameters, and every parameter can be optimised on the historical chart. Even a small grid of ten fast (5 to 50) and 21 slow averages (50 to 250) gives 209 valid combinations. If you test them all and show only the best, the probability of finding, purely by chance, at least one hit that is significant at the 5% level is over 99.99% for independent tests, even in pure noise. Around ten such chance hits are to be expected. However, the tests are not independent, because neighbouring parameters produce almost identical curves. The effective number of trials is therefore smaller than 209, but never smaller than one, and the probability of a chance hit is correspondingly below the value for independent tests.

Because of the multiple testing problem, Harvey, Liu and Zhu (2016) call for a t-statistic above 3.0 instead of the usual 2.0 and sum up the situation as follows: “most claimed research findings in financial economics are likely false”. A backtest metric without stating how many variants were tested is therefore not meaningful. The literature on technical analysis has gone through the same development. Brock, Lakonishok and LeBaron (1992) found strong evidence for simple moving average rules in the Dow for 1897-1986. Sullivan, Timmermann and White (1999) used a bootstrap across the entire universe of rules to correct for data snooping. For 1897-1986 the results withstood this correction, but in the ten years that followed (1987-1996) even the best rule no longer delivered a significant advantage.

bloecke.titel: Choice of parameters and trading costs
bloecke.md: Short parameters generate more signals and thus more round turns. With total costs of 0.10% per round turn (fees for buying and selling, half the spread on each side, slippage), the costs add up to 25 percentage points a year with 250 round turns and to 100 percentage points with 1,000 round turns. Because the costs of each round turn are deducted from the capital remaining at that point, capital at the end of the year is around 22% or around 63% lower, respectively, than without these costs. In addition, there is tax. Gains are subject to the flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer) of 25% under Section 32d(1) EStG (Income Tax Act) plus a solidarity surcharge of 5.5% under Section 4 SolzG 1995 (Solidarity Surcharge Act), so effectively 26.375%. It is often overlooked that indicator software, data feeds, chart subscriptions and trading courses are not tax-deductible. Section 20(9) EStG rules out the deduction of income-related expenses (Werbungskosten) and allows only the saver's allowance (Sparer-Pauschbetrag) of €1,000 (€2,000 for joint assessment).

Before an indicator goes into the chart, four points need to be clarified: which input series it uses and whether another indicator in the chart already uses the same one; how large its average lag in periods is; what exactly an extreme value says when translated back into the original quantity; and how many parameter combinations were tried before this one was left.

mitnehmen: Indicators reshape existing information and generate no new information, which is why three oscillators on the same price series count as only one confirmation.
The average lag follows from the formula and is (n−1)/2 periods for both SMA(n) and EMA(n); the SMA(200) lags about twenty weeks behind, and the RSI(14) behaves like an EMA(27).
A moving average can turn simply because an old price drops out of the window, even if the price does not move today.
An RSI of 70 only means that the average up day was 2.33 times as large as the average down day.
Without stating how many variants were tested, an optimised parameter is merely a selection from noise.

begriffe.text: Weight α with which the current price enters an exponential average. The usual choice is α = 2/(n+1), so that EMA(n) and SMA(n) have the same average lag of (n−1)/2 periods.
Updating an average as (previous value × (n−1) + current value)/n, as used in the RSI and ATR. It corresponds to an EMA with α = 1/n, that is, in EMA notation, to the number of periods 2n−1.
Oscillator between 0 and 100 that indicates the proportion of the average upward movement in the total movement of the last 14 periods. The usual thresholds are 70 and 30.

Distance between the upper and lower Bollinger Bands divided by the middle band. The measure shows how widely the last 20 closing prices were dispersed, not how widely they will be dispersed in future.

Wilder-smoothed average of the true range, that is, the largest of the three ranges formed from the daily high, the daily low and the previous day's close. The ATR is an amount in price units and measures swings, not direction.
Bias that arises when many variants are tested on the same data and only the best is reported. The result is then a selection from chance hits and not a genuine finding.
